findings.location: src/http/binding.ts POST /api/forms/binding (human path) — classifyLayoutSave call at ~line 550
findings.issue: The classifyLayoutSave {root:...}→{type:'root',children:[root]} normalization (extracted from the pre-existing /binding handler) fixes a real latent bug (a real FormDesigner {schemaVersion,source,root:{...}} document previously mis-classified as false-Floor-2, per floor-boundary.ts's B-1 root-bypass contract from T-0519). Verified this is a correctness fix, not a weakening: floor-boundary.ts itself is untouched by this diff (`git diff dev...HEAD -- src/core/floor-boundary.ts` is empty), and its existing `isRoot && type === 'root'` handling is exactly what the wrapper now feeds it. However, there is still no dedicated regression test asserting POST /api/forms/binding (the human path) accepts a real {root:...} layout end-to-end — only the new document-ops wire test exercises classifyLayoutSave's Floor-1 200 case. The author flagged this gap themselves in pr-handoff findings[1]. Low risk (shared code path, machine-seam wire test already proves the gate function works), but should not be dropped.
findings.suggestion: Add a small POST /api/forms/binding test posting a real {schemaVersion,source,root:{type:'section',children:[...]}} layout with fieldKeys present in the live schema and assert 200/201 (not 409). Fast follow-up, not blocking.

findings.issue: The TS server port is a manually-synced mirror of the client JS module (ADR-T0656 §4.1, necessary given tsconfig rootDir:src forbids a runtime web→src import). The shared op-vectors fixture proves behavioral parity for the vectors it covers, but nothing catches a signature/export-name drift (e.g. one module adding a new op function the other lacks) until someone writes a new vector. The author already flagged this exact gap as a finding (pr-handoff findings[2]: 'CI gate asserting identical exported function names').
findings.suggestion: Non-blocking; the existing parity fixture already gives real protection for the 5 ops in the closed vocabulary. Consider the export-name-drift gate as a follow-up task, mirroring forms-schema-binding.sh's drift guard.
